- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) after a peak, model fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast by 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or weak (0.00–0.33) and recent price is trending down; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in mean reversion; if true outcome is below 3-day moving average, model should be adjusted downward by 0.5–1.5%.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to ignore trend; apply a small upward bias if price is trending up, or downward if trending down.
